asker_query: Doctor, I had TB 7 years ago, finished my treatment. Now my lungs have some scarring. I get breathless on stairs. What is the best long-term plan — exercises, any medicines, vaccines? How do I keep my lungs as healthy as possible?
answer:
Managing post-TB pulmonary fibrosis requires a focus on symptom control and preventing further lung strain. While your condition is stable, the scarring (fibrosis) restricts lung expansion, leading to the breathlessness you feel on exertion. For pharmacological management, if your breathlessness worsens, low-dose oral morphine is recognized as highly effective for relieving the sensation of dyspnea by acting on specific centers in the brain. However, this should only be initiated under the guidance of a palliative care physician. Ensure you remain up-to-date with annual influenza and pneumococcal vaccinations to prevent respiratory infections, which can exacerbate scarring. If you experience wheezing, consult your doctor to see if bronchodilators or nebulizers are indicated to open your airways.
For your daily routine, non-pharmacological management is your most powerful tool. You should practice "pursed-lip breathing" and "leaning forward" techniques to improve airflow during exertion. At home, maintain a calm environment, ensure good ventilation by keeping windows open, and use a fan to direct a gentle stream of air toward your face, which can significantly reduce the sensation of breathlessness. If you feel anxious, use relaxation techniques like focusing on pleasant memories or calm scenes. To maintain overall health, continue your diabetes management, as stable blood sugar supports your immune system. If you notice a sudden increase in breathlessness at rest, persistent cough, fever, or if you feel you are "suffocating," these are red flags requiring immediate medical evaluation at your nearest health center.
Caregivers should monitor for signs of respiratory distress and ensure the patient avoids heavy physical strain.
